result.title: Employers can’t find enough workers with these skills
result.description:
‘Maker skills’ are the engine of the global economy. 

These core practical abilities - in construction, operation and resources handling - account for almost half of #employment worldwide. 

But demand is running way ahead of supply, which means in many regions there’s a shortage of people with these skills. In the US, people with maker skills are doing five times as much overtime as other workers, on average.

A new report examines the reasons behind the shortage of makers and offers five major recommendations for how to grow the maker workforce of tomorrow. Read it here: https://www.weforum.org/publications/new-economy-skills-skills-for-the-maker-economy/

result.title: The body’s built-in courier
result.description:
One of the most promising new medical technologies is a natural drug delivery system that could help beat Alzheimer's and other diseases that have been hard to treat for decades.

It relies on exosomes, tiny messenger bubbles created by cells. Kimmy Bettinger explains to Robin Pomeroy how exosomes work.

Watch the full episode on the Top 10 Emerging Technologies 2026 here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2H4pXNZldHs&t=1s

result.title: The global economy is stabilizing. But it’s not all good news, say chief economists
result.description:
Amid geopolitical tensions and the rapid rise of new technologies, what’s the outlook for the global economy?

That’s what we asked some of the planet’s leading chief #economists. Just over half said they expect the global economy to stabilize in the coming year, while 45% expect it to weaken - down from 89% who expected this in May’s survey.

However, the path ahead remains uncertain, due to headwinds including asset-price corrections and global conflict.

Here to talk you through the report’s findings is Philipp Grosskurth, the World Economic Forum’s Insight Lead on Economic Growth.

Read the Chief Economists’ Outlook: September 2026 edition here: https://www.weforum.org/publications/chief-economists-outlook-september-2026

result.title: AI will make organizations more like networks than hierarchiesAccording to Cognizant’s CEO
result.description:
AI isn’t just changing how we work; it could fundamentally change the shape of the organizations we work for.

That’s according to Ravi Kumar, CEO of @Cognizant, which helps companies modernize their technology and reimagine their processes. Kumar believes the traditional corporate pyramid is about to be flattened. By giving workers of all kinds - and at every level - access to powerful new capabilities, he explains how #AI could accelerate the path from entry-level to expertise.

Ravi Kumar was speaking on the World Economic Forum's Radio Davos podcast. Hear the full episode: https://open.spotify.com/episode/3QjJhkcHLrIlr3QcPpXqoT?si=9Nk9LnFVRXCS_2Bx7rg30Q&nd=1&dlsi=b51280d57f734069
